task_1.title: Require compatible importlib-metadata on Python < 3.10
task_1.description: The update raises the minimum supported importlib-metadata version for Python versions earlier than 3.10 so CLI command discovery can use grouped entry point lookup without failing at startup.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that environments running on Python versions earlier than 3.10 install a compatible importlib-metadata release so Flask CLI command discovery does not fail with a TypeError during startup.

expectation.grounded: For Python versions below 3.10, the dependency requirement must enforce importlib-metadata >= 3.6.0. In those environments, Flask CLI plugin and command loading that relies on importlib_metadata.entry_points with grouped lookup must work without raising TypeError because of an incompatible entry_points signature.
expectation.conceptual: Older Python environments should automatically receive a metadata library version that supports the framework's CLI command discovery behavior, so command startup and plugin loading work normally instead of crashing because of dependency incompatibility.

constraints.grounded: The minimum-version requirement change applies only when python_version < 3.10. Behavior for Python 3.10 and newer must remain unchanged, and the update must not alter CLI command discovery semantics beyond removing failures caused by unsupported importlib-metadata versions.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to affected older runtimes, preserve existing command discovery behavior, and avoid introducing new behavior changes for newer Python versions.

behavior: On Python versions earlier than 3.10, installation requires importlib-metadata version 3.6.0 or newer.
CLI command discovery that reads the flask.commands entry point group can execute on affected older Python versions without failing because the metadata library lacks grouped entry point support.
The upgrade removes a runtime startup failure in command resolution caused by an incompatible importlib-metadata API rather than changing the set of commands or plugins that are discovered.
Python 3.10 and newer continue without this backport dependency floor change.
acceptance_criteria: When the package is installed on Python 3.7, 3.8, or 3.9, dependency resolution should select importlib-metadata version 3.6.0 or newer.

When a Flask CLI process starts on Python versions earlier than 3.10, loading commands from the flask.commands entry point group should not fail with TypeError caused by the metadata library's entry_points API.
When CLI command discovery runs in an affected older Python environment, it should continue discovering available commands normally after the dependency upgrade.
When the package is installed on Python 3.10 or newer, this change should not impose a new importlib-metadata backport requirement.
